problem:
Calculate the point where the ellipse  ${x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}+6x+16y+9=0$ intercepts the $x$-axis.

The $x$-intercept is $($
{{field-1}}
,
{{field-2}}$).$
worked_solution:
To calculate the $x$-intercepts, we need to substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the ellipse and solve the resulting equation for $x.$ We do this and solve the resulting equation by completing the square:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}+6x+16y+9 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}+4\cdot {0}^{2}+6x+16\cdot 0+9 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}+6x+9 & =0 \\ (x+3)^{2} & =0 \\ x+3 & =0 \\ x & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the ellipse intercepts the $x$-axis at  $(-3,0).$
